summary: A linked list stores values in separate nodes, each pointing to the next one. Adding at the front is O(1), but reaching index i takes i steps.
notes: while current is not None: is the standard traversal loop. It stops after the last node.
insert_at sets new_node.next before current.next. Reversing those two lines loses the rest of the list.
__str__ is what print() calls to turn the list into text.
pitfall: Calling insert_at with an index past the end makes current become None, and current.next fails with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'next'.
